problem_statement: The HTTP server does not notify an application's dynamic-resource callback when a request has been handled and the response fully delivered to the client. Previously the only terminal callback notification was the abort status, which fires only when the transaction fails part-way through. An application therefore has no signal for a successful completion and cannot release resources (such as a dynamically allocated response buffer) once a response has actually been sent to the client; it must keep those buffers alive for the whole lifetime of the resource. After the change, the server must additionally invoke the dynamic-resource callback one more time, with a distinct terminal status meaning 'response sent completely', exactly once per successful transaction (in addition to the existing abort status), so the application can reset its per-request state and free any dynamically allocated buffers. The status values reported to the callback should also be named to reflect that they describe the overall HTTP transaction (request-data progress, abort, and completion) rather than just data transfer.
